author: reek
body: On x86-64 the compiler fuses a power-of-two remainder compared against zero into a single flag-setting AND: `if math-mod n 2 == 0` lowers to `test v0 #1` and a branch on `eq`, with no division and no remainder anywhere.

author: reek
body: **The plug lanes see the inlined body too, and this file is where that was measured both ways.** Until that was fixed they did not: `compile-frontend` emitted the IR wire straight out of `lower-chapter` without ever calling `run-ir-pipeline`, which only `compile-frontend-cdx` did, so the wire still read `(apply (name "math-mod") ...)` and the plug emitted a real call and a compare against zero. Disassembled on ARM64 at the time: `MOVZ X1,#2; BL math-mod; CMP X9,#0`. Passing `-Passes +inline-leaf-calls` changed nothing, which is what ruled out a flag problem and pinned it on the path. The IR emitters now go through `compile-frontend-ir`, which runs the pipeline; the TEXT emitters do not, because an inlined body is not the definition semantic equivalence compares against. `math-mod` no longer appears in the ARM64 binary's symbol map for this file at all -- inlined, then dropped by dead-code elimination.

author: reek
body: **This file still pins ANSWERS and not a shape, and that is not a leftover.** The lanes reach these answers by different instructions -- x86 fuses to a single `test`, and the ARM64 plug lowers the inlined remainder through its own selector -- so a shape pin here would be a pin on whichever lane wrote it. The answers are what has to agree.

author: reek
body: **`math-mod` is the one that can fuse and `int-mod` is not.** `int-mod` is a builtin call, so it never reaches the fusion; `math-mod` is an ordinary Foreword definition whose body is `a - (a / b) * b`, pure integer arithmetic over its own parameters, which is exactly what `leaf-body-ok` admits.

author: reek
body: Both are chosen so that a guard which wrongly let them fuse changes an ANSWER and not merely a shape: `lt-mod3 6` is 1 and a mask-2 fusion would say 0.

author: reek
body: **The negative arguments are the point of the pair at the end.** A mask and a remainder do not agree in general -- they differ in sign and in value for a negative dividend, because the remainder follows the quotient's rounding and the mask does not. They agree on zero-ness alone, which is exactly and only what the fusion claims. -4 is even and -5 is odd, and the fused form has to say so.
